title: runtime-adaptive-crypto-kms-proxy-design-notebook
content:
Context
-----
Quick personal notebook about a lightweight KMS-proxy that lives in the inference runtime path. Goal: unify how hosted/dedicated/private deployments call into customer KMS/HSMs while giving the serving runtime low-latency, tenant-safe crypto ops (wrap/unwrap, sign, verify, encrypt/decrypt, derive). This is a sketch — lots of open questions.

Problem statement
-----------------
- Services that need per-request crypto (signing responses, wrapping ephemeral keys, token envelopes) currently either: 1) call external KMS per request (latency/cost), or 2) embed HSM clients in each service (ops surface, audit complexity).
- For inference, small-per-request ops (wrap key for session, sign a response stamp) need predictable latency and fault isolation across tenants.

Design goals
------------
1) Tenant isolation: proxy must enforce tenant-specific access policies, ops scoping, and audit logs.
2) Low tail latency: cache safe ephemeral keys and use async/queue for heavy ops.
3) Fail-open/-closed configurable per customer: host teams should be able to tune behavior.
4) Minimal surface: provide a compact REST/gRPC shim that normalizes different vendor KMS APIs.
5) Observability: per-op traces, counts, and cost-estimates (estimated KMS call counts).
6) Deploy modes: hosted (proxy managed by Redwood), dedicated (proxy in customer VPC), private (on-prem proxy package).

Threat model & assumptions
-------------------------
- Proxy does not store long-term plaintext keys. Any long-term secret is always behind customer KMS/HSM.
- Proxy may cache derived ephemeral keys in memory encrypted by process-local key (rotated frequently).
- We assume strong network controls when proxy runs in customer VPC.
- Compromise of proxy host should not reveal customer master keys; it may reveal ephemeral session keys for a window.

High-level flow (ASCII)
-----------------------
Client request                     Runtime KMS-proxy                Customer KMS/HSM
  |                                    |                                   |
  |--- request: wrap-session-key ----->|    (check tenant policy, cache?)     |
  |                                    |--- call: WrapKey / Sign ---------->|
  |                                    |<-- wrappedKey / signature ----------|
  |<-- wrappedKey ---------------------|                                   |

Key operations supported (minimal API)
-------------------------------------
- POST /v1/proxy/wrap { tenant_id, key_id, plaintext_key, ttl, nonce } -> { wrapped_key, meta }
- POST /v1/proxy/unwrap { tenant_id, key_id, wrapped_blob } -> { plaintext_key (ephemeral), meta }
- POST /v1/proxy/sign { tenant_id, key_id, digest, alg } -> { signature }
- POST /v1/proxy/verify { tenant_id, key_id, digest, signature } -> { ok }
- POST /v1/proxy/derive { tenant_id, key_material, context } -> { derived_key }
- GET /v1/proxy/status/{tenant_id} -> { last_kms_sync, cache_hit_rate }

Notes on API shape: keep request/response JSON small. Accept base64 for blobs. Support optional ttl_ms for ephemeral keys and allow a request-scoped nonce to prevent replay.

Runtime-local caching & safety
-----------------------------
- Cache wrapped artifacts (wrappedKey -> unwrapped plaintext in memory) but encrypt in-process using a rotating process key that is loaded from KMS at startup (so compromise of machine without KMS compromise yields limited window).
- Cache policy: per-tenant LRU with size and TTL caps. Evict proactively under memory pressure.

Adaptive behavior idea
----------------------
- Use operator-configured heuristics to decide when to call customer KMS vs serve from cache vs re-derive via local algorithm (for derivable keys). Heuristics sample: qps, p95 KMS latency, error rate, estimated cost per KMS call.
- Runtime exposes a small policy DSL: e.g., "if kms_p95 > 120ms and cache_hit_rate > 0.3 then allow_stale_from-cache=true;" Implement as a simple rule engine (json/yaml).

Failure modes and fallback
-------------------------
- KMS unavailable: fallbacks = [cached-ephemeral, derive-local (if allowed), fail-hard]. Policy per-tenant.
- Partial failure on wrap: log, increment span, return 503 with structured body indicating fallback used.

Audit & compliance hooks
------------------------
- Emit audit records per-tenant with operation, key_id, caller, outcome, latency. Ship to central audit pipeline (or local file for on-prem).
- Support on-demand proof-of-rotation: store per-op fingerprint (not plaintext) that can be pushed to customer audit.

Config schema (sketch)
----------------------
{ "tenant_id": "string", "kms_bindings": [{ "key_id": "string", "provider": "aws|gcp|azure|hsm", "uri": "string" }], "cache": { "max_entries": 1024, "entry_ttl_ms": 300000 }, "fallback_policy": { "on_kms_failure": "use_cache|derive|fail" }, "adaptive_rules": [ {"name": "latency_guard", "expr": "kms_p95_ms > 150 && cache_hit_rate > 0.2", "action": "allow_cache_stale" } ] }

Instrumentation & telemetry
-------------------------
- Per-op tags: tenant_id, op_type, key_family, fallback_used (bool), cache_hit (bool).
- Metrics to export: kms_calls_total, kms_call_latencies_ms (histogram), cache_hits_total, ephemeral_keys_live.
- Trace example: start-span(proxy.wrap) -> annotate upstream_kms_span_id -> finish.

Operational concerns
--------------------
- Key rotation: on rotation event, proxy must evict matching cached items and optionally prewarm new wrapped blobs by calling KMS asynchronously.
- Secrets for process-local encryption must be pulled from KMS at boot; for dedicated/private we provide an operator hook to mount a sealed secret.
- Backpressure: if KMS call queue grows, proxy should return 429 or apply tenant-priority throttling.

Open questions / TODOs
---------------------
- Should the proxy accept tenant-supplied signing algorithms, or normalize to a small set? (compat vs safety)
- Replay prevention granularity: per-wrap nonce, or attach timestamp + signature from runtime?
- Cost accounting: how to pass cost attribution to billing pipeline (estimate per-op vs exact from provider).
- Security review request: run threat-model with security team, especially around in-memory plaintext exposure window.
- Prototype: build a minimal Go service implementing wrap/unwrap + caching + simple policy engine; target p95 < 30ms for cache path, < 120ms for KMS path.

Notes to self
------------
- Start with AWS and generic HSM binder; later expand to GCP/Azure interfaces.
- Keep API intentionally small and composable; runtime will call wrapping on session create and signing on response emit.
- Put an example integration in the serving-runtime repo under examples/kms-proxy-client.

References and sketches
----------------------
- Related internal threads: slack #serving-runtime: thread KMS-proxy (link omitted)
- Confluence draft: CONFLUENCE-3452 (linked above)

End of notebook (work-in-progress).
